## Natural history notes

A small crambid moth characterized by narrow straw-colored to brownish wings with subtle darker lines and mottling, giving it the typical grass-moth appearance. In Florida, it is found in marshes, wet prairies, roadsides, fields, pine flatwoods, and other open habitats where grasses, sedges, or reed-like plants are available. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights, while the caterpillars are stem-borers or concealed feeders in grasses and related plants, helping move wetland and grassland vegetation into the broader food web for spiders, birds, bats, and parasitoid wasps.
